gates.title: Per-image licensing, archive capture, and public availability
gates.plan_assumption_checked: ASSET_PLAN.md:120 says the shot 'may need YouTube archival footage or AI-generated stand-in'. Checked: a YouTube-hosted clip carries no reuse permission, so YouTube leads are rights-blocked. Free stock (Pexels, Pixabay, Mixkit, Coverr) has no genuine 1990s software store footage. Archive-hosted home video exists with an uploader-asserted CC0.

producer_ruling.decided_by: Devin (sole human reviewer), relayed through the B-roll Scouting Manager
producer_ruling.ruling: The Internet Archive item page states CC0 1.0 Universal. That CC0 dedication was applied by the Internet Archive uploader 'The Nostalgist777', not by the filmmaker Dan Lynch. Devin accepted that uploader-applied CC0 as-is on 2026-09-15 and ruled that filmmaker permission will not be pursued.
producer_ruling.effect_on_H02a: Handoff item H02-a is closed as 'not pursued by decision'. It is NOT closed as 'permission obtained'; the filmmaker did not license this footage and was not contacted.
producer_ruling.effect_on_this_gate: This ruling settles the licensing basis for acquisition and for keeping the file in the repo. It does not clear the asset for release. R14 stays `open` and release_status stays `blocked` until the OPS-04 review deck, because the residual risk below and the recognizable-people question are unresolved.
producer_ruling.residual_risk_recorded: Creative Commons states it 'has not verified the copyright status of any work to which CC0 has been applied'. The Internet Archive states it 'does not make guarantees as to the copyright status of items on archive.org'. Devin accepted that risk on 2026-09-15.

gates.boundary_compliance: One approved file downloaded (candidate 1), with a generic browser User-Agent and no personal data in the request. No account created, no terms accepted, no payment, no CAPTCHA bypass (stopped at UNT and Pond5), no watermark removal. Candidates 2 and 3 were not downloaded.
settled_since_scouting: Legal basis for candidate 1: settled by Devin's 2026-09-15 ruling (uploader-applied CC0 accepted as-is; filmmaker permission not pursued). No longer a review question.
review_questions: Legal risk / privacy: the home video shows identifiable members of the public and store staff. Is that acceptable as incidental B-roll? Sharpened by the acquisition pass: the frames at 00:02:22.5-00:02:24.0 give clear, frontal, identifiable faces of a CompUSA employee (name badge visible) and a customer, so the answer partly determines the out point.

Editorial: the real file shows the scouted out point 00:02:24.0 does not hold - the browse ends about 00:02:22.5 and 02:23-02:24 becomes a two-man handshake. Take the recommended 6.5 s cut (02:16.0-02:22.5, under the ticket's preferred 8-12 s), keep the 8.0 s cut including the interaction, or use the alternate 00:03:26.0-00:03:36.0 segment?

Taste: the footage is launch-night event footage (balloons, crowd, a promoter in a Microsoft Office box costume), not a quiet everyday browse. Does that fit script sections 3 and 12, or does it read as 'Windows 95 launch' rather than 'buying software in the 90s'?

Taste / technical: measured on the real file, the active picture is only 632x480 pillarboxed inside the 854x480 container. Filling 1920x1080 is about a 2.25x upscale. Pillarbox the upscaled 4:3 picture on the 1080p timeline, crop to 16:9 and accept the softening, or present it in an authored archival frame treatment? (Stretching to 16:9 is not an option.)
Audio: the file carries an opus stereo track, not auditioned. Use the segment mute, or audition it first for speech, music or store PA that may carry separate rights?
Cost: is licensing the 1993 KXAS broadcast clip (beginning rate $90/second, not viewed) still worth pursuing now that candidate 1 is acquired? Presumed no.
Scope: if the acquired footage is rejected on review, does Devin want a separately approved and labeled AI stand-in or staged reenactment assignment? (Not commissioned by this ticket.)
